_comment: Funders spotted but not yet watched. Two ways in: the daily sweep meets a funder through an aggregator that is not in sources.json, and a weekly pass searches for newly launched funds. Nothing here reaches the site. A candidate becomes a source only when a person moves it into sources.json — an automated list that adds its own sources would eventually add a scam, and the only thing this site has is being trustworthy.

candidates.name: National Institute for Health Care Management (NIHCM) Foundation
candidates.why: Funds annual US health-care journalism grants of $15,000-$30,000 for independent journalists and newsrooms.

candidates.name: Media Innovation Europe (International Press Institute consortium)
candidates.why: Funds European media organisations' audience-engagement and business-innovation projects.

candidates.name: Henry Nxumalo Foundation / SA|AJP
candidates.why: Provides investigative-journalism reporting grants and editorial support to journalists and newsrooms across the SADC region.

candidates.name: Batory Foundation / EEA & Norway Grants Civil Society Fund Poland
candidates.why: Administers Polish civil-society grants including calls for projects countering disinformation, some of which fund media literacy/journalism activity.

candidates.name: Tech Policy Press
candidates.why: Funds a $10,000, year-long fellowship for journalists, researchers and policy professionals reporting on tech and democracy.

candidates.name: International Journalists' Programmes (IJP)
candidates.why: Runs recurring German-Northern European and German-British (Weidenfeld) journalist exchange fellowships, each with a €3,800 scholarship.

candidates.name: World Federation of Science Journalists / WCSJ2027
candidates.why: Travel fellowships for journalists and journalism students to attend the World Conference of Science Journalists.

candidates.name: Exile Hub
candidates.why: Runs the Critical Voices Fellowship and other emergency/production funds for exiled Myanmar media professionals.

candidates.name: Durham University - Sir Harry Evans Memorial Fund
candidates.why: Nine-month early-career investigative journalism fellowship placed inside a Reuters newsroom.

candidates.name: Nova Institute for Health
candidates.why: Funds a $60,000 one-year health-journalism fellowship for US journalists.

candidates.name: Walkley Foundation
candidates.why: Australian journalism foundation that co-administers and hosts grant programmes for freelance journalists.

candidates.name: Fundación Avina
candidates.why: Latin American foundation that co-funds Fundación Gabo's investigative-journalism grants on sustainable-development themes.

candidates.name: The Climate Pledge
candidates.why: Co-funds, with the National Geographic Society, storytelling grants (up to $100,000) for journalists and other storytellers covering climate resilience, energy transition and sustainability.

candidates.name: Fulbright-National Geographic Digital Storytelling Fellowship (via Fulbright/IIE)
candidates.why: A joint Fulbright/National Geographic award funding US citizens to combine an academic research grant abroad with digital storytelling/multimedia journalism training.

candidates.name: Reflecta Fördermittelkompass
candidates.why: A German funding database that aggregates media/journalism grant and scholarship listings not otherwise indexed by the existing aggregator sources.

candidates.name: Africa No Filter
candidates.why: Runs the Voices for Climate Justice Program, an adjacent-track grant explicitly open to journalists producing climate-justice content in ten African countries.

candidates.name: German Embassy Kyiv
candidates.why: Funds a recurring Ukrainian human-rights project call with a press/media-freedom and disinformation priority area, restricted to Ukrainian media organisations.

candidates.name: Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ) Foundation
candidates.why: US journalism nonprofit's foundation running an annual grant cycle for journalists/newsrooms plus a small members-only Freelance Fund mini-grant.

candidates.name: Media Diversity Institute (Western Balkans)
candidates.why: Runs journalism-adjacent media literacy/gender programmes in the Western Balkans (currently the MLADI Award, a prize, so not recorded as a grant); may run other applicable funding.

candidates.name: Public Interest Journalism Lab (PIJL)
candidates.why: Runs an emergency/operational grants programme (several open calls per year, plus a 2026 scholarship call with ECPMF) for Ukrainian regional media outlets and individual journalists, prioritising frontline regions.

candidates.name: The Fix Media Foundation — Technology Support Fund
candidates.why: Runs an equipment grant scheme replacing lost or outdated gear for journalists working in frontline or high-risk areas in Ukraine/Eastern Europe. Note: a separate URL from the already-tracked 'thefix.media' source (The Fix media innovation programmes) — may be a related but distinct foundation entity worth checking.

candidates.name: The Lenfest Institute for Journalism
candidates.why: Runs its own journalism funding programmes (e.g. Lenfest-Google News Initiative News Catalyst Grants for local news community-listening projects) beyond the Google co-branded one.

candidates.name: African Investigative Journalism Conference (AIJC)
candidates.why: Runs an annual, francophone-focused, fully-funded conference fellowship for investigative journalists in Africa.

candidates.name: Harold W. McGraw, Jr. Center for Business Journalism
candidates.why: Runs a recurring (spring/fall) $15,000 business-journalism reporting fellowship open to freelance and staff journalists.

candidates.name: Journalism Science Alliance
candidates.why: EJC-hosted, EUR 2.7 million, two-year programme (2025-2027) delivering grant funding, training, mentoring and networking for science-backed investigative journalism; annual call cycle, currently closed for 2026.

candidates.name: International Fund for Public Interest Media (IFPIM)
candidates.why: Global multilateral fund making grants up to US$250,000 to independent public-interest media organisations in low- and middle-income countries across Africa, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Eastern Europe.
candidates.evidence: ifpim.org and gfmd.info funding archive; IFJ (ifj.org) press release, 1 Aug 2026, on the IFPIM-funded $1m Palestine media fund it distributes through the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: RCDIJ Africa Fund (Ripples Centre for Data and Investigative Journalism)
candidates.why: Nigeria-based nonprofit's pan-African fund of up to US$10,000 for individual journalists' data and investigative journalism projects.
candidates.evidence: Media Rights Agenda (mediarightsagenda.org) and gfmd.info funding-archive coverage of the 2026 RCDIJ Africa Fund call; confirmed on rcdij.org. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: St. David's Foundation
candidates.why: Central Texas health foundation funding local newsrooms and community-centered journalism covering health and social issues affecting underserved communities, through its 'Strengthening Local Media to Advance Community Health' programme.
candidates.evidence: stdavidsfoundation.org 2026 grantmaking announcement naming 21 organisations awarded over $3m under the local-media funding opportunity. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: Journalists for Human Rights (JHR)
candidates.why: Canadian media-development NGO training journalists in 23 countries to report on human rights, democratic reform and climate, with small reporting grants available to journalists who complete its training.
candidates.evidence: opportunitiesforyouth.org write-up of the 2026 JHR Program (training plus small reporting grants, deadline 10 Aug 2026), confirmed against jhr.ca. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: Solutions Journalism Network
candidates.why: Co-runs journalism fellowships with other funders (e.g. the European media leaders climate solutions fellowship with EJC) and posts fellowship calls on its own site.

candidates.name: European Media and Information Fund (EMIF)
candidates.why: Gulbenkian-hosted fund running open calls for media literacy, disinformation research and journalism-adjacent projects across Europe; surfaced while researching the EEA Grants Romania disinformation call. Not verified in depth — flagged for a future dedicated check.

candidates.name: Alfred Friendly Press Partners
candidates.why: Runs a six-month fellowship placing early-career journalists (aged 25-35, 3+ years' experience) from developing countries in U.S. newsrooms via the Missouri School of Journalism, with a $2,000 living stipend and essentials covered, plus a separate four-week programme for journalists living in exile in the US. Surfaced as a Scholars at Risk 'Practitioners at Risk' host-institution partner.

candidates.name: Digital Forensic Research Lab (DFRLab), Atlantic Council
candidates.why: Runs Digital Sherlocks, a free annual training programme for journalists/civil society on monitoring and protecting the information environment, listed as a media opportunity via IJNet.

candidates.name: Climate Justice Resilience Fund (CJRF)
candidates.why: Explicitly funds documentation, journalism, oral histories and visual storytelling as part of its climate-justice grantmaking to frontline communities — a much closer match to the 'climate-justice-resilience' source's own name and stated purpose than the currently configured ClimateWorks Foundation URL, which is invitation-only and unrelated to media. Worth tracking as its own source.

candidates.name: FRIDA — The Young Feminist Fund
candidates.why: Global feminist fund listed on Global Fund for Women's own funder-resources page; young-feminist-led groups doing storytelling/media work could plausibly fit the adjacent track.

candidates.name: Equality Fund
candidates.why: Global feminist funder now confirmed (via GFMD) to run its own Global Journalism Fellowship 2026-2027 (CAD 4,000, five fellows from ODA-recipient countries), in partnership with CJFE and AWiM; already a tracked candidate (previously seenAt global-fund-for-women) -- add gfmd-fellowships to its seenAt list rather than duplicating.

candidates.name: AmplifyChange
candidates.why: Funder of sexual and reproductive rights advocacy listed on Global Fund for Women's funder-resources page; advocacy-communications grants may be adjacent-track eligible.

candidates.name: Africa Women's Development Fund (AWDF)
candidates.why: Pan-African feminist fund listed on Global Fund for Women's funder-resources page; not yet assessed for media/documentation eligibility.

candidates.name: Joan Shorenstein Fellowship Program (Shorenstein Center, Harvard Kennedy School)
candidates.why: A one-year (mostly remote) fellowship for journalists with 10+ years' experience to research public policy/political affairs at Harvard; surfaced during today's gijn-grants search fallback.

candidates.name: Press Forward
candidates.why: A $500M+ philanthropic collaborative funding U.S. local news outlets directly (e.g. its 2025 Open Call awarded ~$100k each to 200+ small newsrooms); it also co-funds IWMF's Safety Ambassador Fellowship, and its own Pooled Fund/Open Call cycles could be a distinct grant source worth tracking.

candidates.name: UN Trust Fund to End Violence against Women and Girls (UNTF)
candidates.why: The actual grant-making body behind UN Women's largest civil-society calls for proposals (four-year core/flexible grants, up to ~USD 20M per round across two cohorts) — a more useful source URL than sources.json's current un-women procurement page, which is for vendor procurement, not grants.

candidates.name: Kosovar Civil Society Foundation (KCSF)
candidates.why: Co-manages the Civic Emergency Fund with Trag Foundation and runs its own recurring 'Urgent Grants' open call for Kosovo/regional civil society, which may independently be usable by media/journalism organisations under threat.

candidates.name: Climate Tracker
candidates.why: Runs recurring regional climate-journalism fellowships/reporting grants (e.g. a Latin America solutions-journalism fellowship, stipend up to US$1,000, deadline 16 Feb 2026) surfaced via Terra Viva Grants; not currently open, no entry added, but worth tracking as its own source.

candidates.name: British Council Serbia
candidates.why: UK-Serbia arts/culture co-creation grants (up to GBP 15,000) surfaced while researching the British Embassy Belgrade funding landscape; a distinct funder from the Embassy itself and not currently tracked as its own source.

candidates.name: Digital Whistleblowing Fund (Hermes Center / Renewable Freedom Foundation)
candidates.why: Micro-grants of up to €3,000 plus IT/advisory support for investigative-journalism groups and human-rights grassroots organisations starting secure digital whistleblowing initiatives, requiring endorsement by a partner such as ICIJ, OCCRP or Transparency International.
candidates.evidence: Listed on GIJN's grants & fellowships resource page (surfaced via WebSearch since gijn.org returned HTTP 403 today); most corroborating search results date to ~2020, so current-cycle status is uncertain. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: CTRL+J
candidates.why: Runs Luminate-backed microgrants (US$1,000-5,000) for small convenings on journalism and technology, plus a separate Research Hub for Global South researchers; not yet in sources.json.

candidates.name: CIJI — Collaborative and Investigative Journalism Initiative
candidates.why: EU-funded consortium (partner: Free Press Unlimited) coordinating cross-border investigative journalism grant calls, e.g. the 2026 'cross-border investigations on the impact of AI' grants; may run further calls independently of Free Press Unlimited's own listing.

candidates.name: E3J — European Excellence Exchange in Journalism
candidates.why: EU-funded project (partner: Free Press Unlimited) that has run small production-grant calls (e.g. EUR 10,000 grants for cross-border stories on climate, migration and public health); last known round closed September 2024, current cycle status unconfirmed.

candidates.name: Sudan Media Forum (SMF)
candidates.why: Coalition of independent Sudanese media outlets that jointly launches funding calls with Free Press Unlimited (e.g. 2026 content-production retainers of EUR 1,000 each for 60 individual journalists); worth watching as a co-administering body even though it is not itself the primary funder.

candidates.name: Mongabay
candidates.why: Environmental-journalism nonprofit that co-funds One World Media's Amazon Film Grant (up to $5,000 for documentaries on the Amazon rainforest ecosystem) and may run its own independent journalism-funding programmes.

candidates.name: CITE (Centre for Innovation and Technology, Zimbabwe)
candidates.why: Runs an annual investigative-journalism grants call (up to US$800 per story) for journalists reporting on Zimbabwean communities.
